<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>## Audit Verdict: `platform_writes`/`optional_dep_updates` dispatch loops in `apply_version_plan` (commit `2d53001`)

### Context that changes the risk calculus

Before the specific findings: `plan.platform_writes` and `plan.optional_dep_updates` are **never populated with real data anywhere in the codebase today**. The only real producer of a `VersionPlan`, `plan_version` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:246-258`, hardcodes:
```rust
platform_writes: Vec::new(),
optional_dep_updates: Vec::new(),
```
Same for `commands/snapshot.rs:132-133` and `commands/pr_body.rs:282-283/303-304`. The only place these fields are ever populated with non-empty data is the one new test added in `2d53001` (`apply.rs:2240`). So **this is currently dead code in production** — the loops added in `2d53001` cannot execute with real content via any CLI command today. This matters: it means nothing below is exploitable *yet*, but it's exactly the kind of gap that becomes live the moment someone wires a producer (e.g. a future "platform package" cascade step) into `platform_writes`/`optional_dep_updates` without re-auditing `apply_version_plan`.

### 1. Data-loss/clobber risk from the two independent open→persist cycles

**Not real, given today's structure — verified by tracing `open()`.** `crates/callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs:155-181` (`open()`) does no caching: every call does `CargoToml::open`/`PackageJson::open`/`PyprojectToml::open`, each of which reads the file fresh from disk (confirmed no in-memory cache, no shared mutable state across calls — only a test-observability `AtomicUsize` counter). `apply_version_plan` is fully synchronous, single-threaded, with no deferred/lazy writes — `classify_manifest_writes`'s batched loop (`apply.rs:140-179`), the excluded-bump loop (`181-215`), the excluded-rewrite loop (`217-242`), then `platform_writes` (`244-252`), then `optional_dep_updates` (`254-262`) run strictly in that order, each `persist()` (`callisto-manifests` `atomic_write`) completing before the next loop's `open()` runs. So if the same manifest path appeared in both a batched write and `platform_writes`, the second `open()` would read the first loop's already-persisted bytes — no clobber. The `classify_manifest_writes` invariant (open-once-per-batch) exists to prevent multiple writes *within a single classify group* interleaving on one handle; it says nothing about, and is not violated by, two temporally-sequential open/persist cycles on the same file, because re-opening always re-reads truth from disk.

### 2. Unsafe interleaving relative to batched writes

None found. There is no threading, no async, no reordering of `plan.platform_writes` vs `plan.bumps` — the four loops execute in fixed source order every time. This part of the original architectural worry is not present in the current code.

### 3. Partial-failure behavior

Consistent with (not worse than) the rest of `apply_version_plan` — none of the loops in this function have transactional/rollback semantics; every one (`classify_manifest_writes`'s batched loop, the excluded-bump loop, the excluded-rewrite loop, and now `platform_writes`/`optional_dep_updates`) propagates the first error via `?` and returns early, leaving whatever was already `persist()`ed on disk and skipping git staging entirely (the staging code at `apply.rs:433-470` never runs on early return). This is the established, accepted design in this file (see the `apply_is_idempotent_when_manifest_already_at_target_version` test at `apply.rs:934` — recovery is via re-running `apply_version_plan`, not rollback). One real divergence: the sibling bump loops validate a precondition (`current == bump.from` / `current == bump.to`, else `GraphError::UnexpectedManifestVersion`) before writing, giving crash-recovery detection of "is disk in the state I expect." The new `platform_writes` loop has no `from` field on `PlatformWrite` at all and unconditionally calls `write_version` every time regardless of current on-disk content — it can silently overwrite a manifest version that drifted from the plan's expectation (e.g. a manual edit made between plan computation and apply) with no error, whereas every sibling loop in this same function would catch that and refuse. This is a genuine but currently-dormant (only reachable once the field is wired up) weakening of an established invariant — worth a Medium finding, not urgent given the dead-code status.

### 4. Missing input validation / error-case coverage

- `ManifestFormat::from_path` (`crates/callisto-model/src/package.rs:216-234`) only recognizes a fixed allow-list of filenames (`Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, `go.mod`, `pom.xml`, `deno.json(c)`); anything else — malformed path, no filename, or a lockfile-named path — returns `Err(UnknownManifestFormat)`, propagated cleanly via `?`. Not silent.
- `open()` only actually constructs handles for `CargoToml`/`PackageJson`/`PyprojectToml`; every other recognized format hits the `other =&gt;` arm and returns `Err(ReadOnlyFormat)`. Also visible, not silent.
- The `Manifest` trait (`callisto-manifests/src/lib.rs:26-63`) requires `write_version` and `update_optional_dependencies` as non-default methods on every implementor — so "manifest format doesn't support this operation" cannot happen for any openable format today; this specific worry from the task brief doesn't materialize given the trait's design.
- `npm.rs`'s `update_optional_dependencies` (`npm.rs:353-373`) auto-creates the `optionalDependencies` section if missing and inserts/overwrites unconditionally for every `(name, version)` pair — it never errors on an unknown/new dependency name (unlike `update_dependency_spec`, which does error via `DependencyNotFound`). This is a real asymmetry but is arguably intentional (adding a brand-new optional dep is exactly what a platform-package flow needs) — flagged as undertested, not a bug.
- All of the above are genuinely untested for `platform_writes`/`optional_dep_updates` specifically (only the one happy-path test exists) but none is a live silent-wrong-data-written bug given the trait/format guarantees already in place.

### 5. Does `modified_paths`/staging correctly reflect what happened

Yes for the paths themselves — in both new loops, `modified_paths.push(...)` is the last statement, reached only after `write_version?` and `persist?` both returned `Ok`. No partial-failure-then-staged scenario for the manifest paths.

**However, a real bug exists one layer up:** the `active_ecosystems` computation (`apply.rs:325-349`) that drives both lockfile *refresh* (`354-408`) and lockfile *staging* (`412-431`) is derived **exclusively from `plan.bumps`** — it never inspects `plan.platform_writes` or `plan.optional_dep_updates`. Concretely: a plan containing only `platform_writes`/`optional_dep_updates` entries (exactly the shape of the new happy-path test, which has no `bumps` at all) produces an empty `active_ecosystems` set, so:
- `opts.refresh_lockfiles: true` will never trigger `npm`/`cargo`/`uv`/`poetry` lockfile regeneration for these writes, and
- the corresponding lockfile (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `Cargo.lock`, etc.) will never be added to `modified_paths`/`staged` even if it exists on disk and is now stale relative to the optionalDependencies change just written.

This is a confirmed, code-traced correctness gap in the new feature (Silent Fallback / Spec Drift class) — currently dormant only because nothing populates these plan fields yet.

---

### Findings summary

**[Medium] `platform_writes`/`optional_dep_updates` are excluded from `active_ecosystems`, so their writes never trigger lockfile refresh or lockfile staging**
- Status: CONFIRMED (code-traced, currently dormant — no production producer populates these fields yet)
- Location: `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:244-262` (the new loops) vs. `apply.rs:325-349` (`active_ecosystems`, sourced only from `plan.bumps`)
- Root cause: `active_ecosystems` is computed before/independent of the new loops and never consults `pw.manifest`/`opt.manifest`'s ecosystem.
- Failing scenario: a `VersionPlan` with only `optional_dep_updates` touching `package.json`'s `optionalDependencies`, `refresh_lockfiles: true`, and a real `pnpm-lock.yaml` on disk — `pnpm-lock.yaml` is neither regenerated nor staged, silently drifting from `package.json`.
- Verification strategy: a test asserting `outcome.staged` includes the ecosystem lockfile when only `platform_writes`/`optional_dep_updates` are set (no `bumps`) — fails today, would pass once `active_ecosystems` also folds in these two fields' manifest paths.

**[Medium] `platform_writes` loop has no precondition/invariant check, unlike every sibling write loop in the same function**
- Status: CONFIRMED (code-traced, currently dormant)
- Location: `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:244-252`; contrast with `apply.rs:146-161` and `192-205`, both of which check `current == expected` and raise `GraphError::UnexpectedManifestVersion` on drift.
- Root cause: `PlatformWrite` carries no `from`/expected-current field; the loop calls `handle.write_version(&amp;pw.version, permit)?` unconditionally.
- Failing scenario: a platform manifest's on-disk version was hand-edited (or already correctly bumped by a previous partial run to a *different* value than the plan expects) between plan computation and apply — the loop silently overwrites it with the plan's `pw.version`, with no error and no way for the caller to detect drift, whereas an identical scenario in the batched/bump loops would correctly fail closed.
- Verification strategy: write a test with a platform manifest at an unexpected version and assert this either errors or is intentionally documented as "always authoritative" — currently neither is true; it's just silently unconditional.

**[Low] `update_optional_dependencies` (npm) has no missing-dependency validation, unlike `update_dependency_spec`**
- Status: PLAUSIBLE / by-design ambiguity, not confirmed as a bug
- Location: `crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs:353-373`
- Note: likely intentional (adding new optional deps is the whole point), but undertested for the new call site — worth a regression test locking in the intended behavior explicitly rather than leaving it implicit.

**[Testing gap, not a bug] Only one happy-path test exists for `platform_writes`/`optional_dep_updates`**
- No coverage for: precondition/UnexpectedManifestVersion-style drift, `open()`/`from_path` failure paths, partial-failure mid-loop (first entry persists, second errors), or the `active_ecosystems`/lockfile-staging gap above.

### Is the sequential-execution safety real or illusory?

**Real**, for the specific "stale-handle-clobber" concern the task asked about — `open()`'s unconditional fresh-disk-read plus strictly sequential, single-threaded execution genuinely prevents the two-independent-cycles-race scenario `classify_manifest_writes` was built to guard against. There is no live data-loss/clobber bug here today.

### Ship-readiness

Safe enough to leave as-is with a follow-up hardening task — **but only because the feature is currently unreachable dead code** (no producer populates `platform_writes`/`optional_dep_updates`). Nothing here needs an immediate fix for today's `main`. However, before any future work wires a real producer into these fields, the two Medium findings above (lockfile-staging blind spot, missing precondition check) should be fixed first — otherwise the feature will ship with a real, user-visible stale-lockfile bug and a silently-unconditional-overwrite behavior inconsistent with the rest of the function's crash-safety story.

## The finding that matters most

The spec's line numbers are accurate — I checked every one, and the earlier canon-verifier/canon-auditor corrections did land. But the spec diagnoses bug 1 in the wrong function.

`solve_cascade` already contains a **Linked**-group convergence block at `crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:314-379`: it iterates `input.groups.linked.values()`, computes one shared `winner` version, assigns it to every member, and sets `changed = true` so the outer `while changed` loop re-converges. **There is no Fixed-group counterpart.** That missing block is the bug.

The spec instead targets `raise()`'s sibling loop at `cascade.rs:464-478`, which cannot fix AC-001's scenario:

```rust
// cascade.rs:198 — seeded packages get targets here, before raise() ever runs
for (id, &amp;sev) in input.seed {
    let t = bump_target(id, sev, &amp;input)?;
    out.targets.insert(id.clone(), t);
}

// cascade.rs:464-466 — and the sibling loop is gated on a strict inequality
for sib in groups.fixed_siblings(pkg) {
    let sib_sev = out.severities.get(sib).copied().unwrap_or(Severity::None);
    if sev &gt; sib_sev {   // both siblings at Minor =&gt; false =&gt; body never runs
```

Two siblings both seeded Minor take the line-198 path and never reach `raise()`; even if they did, `sev &gt; sib_sev` is false. BLK-01 is the blocker to fix first — BLK-02 through BLK-07 are downstream of it or independent smaller defects.

The central judgment call the task asked me to make on evidence, not assumption: I traced `fixed_group_target`, `pre_mutation_checks`, and the new/existing convergence blocks in `solve_cascade` line by line for what happens if a group's `members` Vec contains the same `PackageId` twice (two spellings). In every one of these paths, the aggregation is keyed by `PackageId` and is either a `max()` over repeated equal values, an equality-gated `insert` (`if out.targets.get(&amp;id) != Some(&amp;winner)`), or feeds a `BTreeSet` worklist — all naturally idempotent under a repeated key. A duplicated member does not corrupt `AC-001`/`AC-002`'s target computation or `AC-007`'s divergence detection; it only causes harmless redundant iteration. That contradicts the premise embedded in AC-010c's justification, so I'm treating the dedup requirement as scope creep the drafter rationalized into self-consistency (by amending non_goals) rather than a necessity proven from the other criteria.

```json
{
  "issues": [
    {
```
```json
      "criterion_id": "AC-002",
      "type": "ambiguous",
      "description": "The criterion says PlatformWrite.from is read 'via the platform manifest's own current_version()' but never specifies which ManifestRole plan_version must pass into ManifestDecl::new when opening path P. This is not a cosmetic gap: GroupMember::PlatformManifest carries its own `role: ManifestRole` field (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs:28-33), and existing code (crates/callisto-graph/src/groups.rs:186-199) genuinely populates that field with ManifestRole::Platform{platform, arch, abi} for real platform-package members. ManifestDecl::new (crates/callisto-model/src/package.rs:88-107) actively rejects that combination: `if matches!(role, ManifestRole::Platform{..}) &amp;&amp; format == ManifestFormat::CargoToml { return Err(invalid_role_for_format) }`. So an implementer who does the 'obvious' thing -- thread the GroupMember's own role field through to open the manifest at plan time -- will get a spurious construction error for any Cargo/TOML-formatted platform manifest (a real maturin/Rust platform-package layout, the same class of scenario AC-007 calls out for napi-rs). A second implementer who instead hardcodes ManifestRole::Canonical (mirroring how apply.rs's existing platform_writes dispatch loop already opens the exact same path at apply.rs:247, and optional_dep_updates at apply.rs:257) will not hit this and will produce different, correct behavior. ### Blocker 1 — AC-009 and AC-010 assert a refresh that does not exist (disqualifying on its own)
```

`apply.rs:353-407` has exactly two refresh branches: `active_ecosystems.contains(&amp;Ecosystem::Cargo)` (line 356, `cargo update --workspace`) and `Ecosystem::Pypi` (line 372, `uv lock` / `poetry lock --no-update`). **There is no `Ecosystem::Npm` branch anywhere.** No npm refresh subprocess is ever run and no npm entry ever enters `refresh_results`.

What npm actually gets today is *staging only*: the table at `apply.rs:411-421` maps package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, bun.lockb to `Ecosystem::Npm`, and `apply.rs:423-431` pushes each that exists on disk into `modified_paths`. That table is **not** filtered by the detected npm workspace kind, so AC-009's "matching the detected npm workspace kind" also misdescribes the mechanism.

AC-009's clause "exactly as it already is for an ordinary plan.bumps-only plan touching an npm manifest" is therefore false. The implementer must choose between (a) implementing only the `active_ecosystems` extension the scope authorizes — leaving the "refreshed" clause permanently unsatisfiable — or (b) inventing an npm refresh command the spec never names, which is outside the stated scope. Required change: split refresh from staging, assert `ApplyOutcome.staged` contains the npm lockfiles present at root and `ApplyOutcome.lockfile_refresh_results` contains no npm entry; same rewrite for AC-010. If an npm refresh is genuinely wanted it needs its own spec — it is a third distinct change on top of this track's two fixes.

### Blocker 2 — AC-002 stops one step short of making its own motivating case work

The auditor's `ManifestRole::Canonical` fix is correct as far as it goes — I confirmed `apply.rs:247` and `apply.rs:257` both use it, and `package.rs:104-106` really does reject Platform-role + CargoToml. But:

- `ManifestDecl::new` does not open anything (`package.rs:88-113`); it validates a path/role/format triple. The opener is `callisto_manifests::open(&amp;decl, &amp;ctx)` (`lib.rs:155`), requiring an `OpenContext { workspace_root, cargo_workspace, npm_workspace_kind }` (`lib.rs:103-108`). AC-002 as written is not a runnable sequence.
- AC-002 never says what `cargo_workspace` plan_version passes, and that choice flips the outcome for the exact scenario AC-002 cites. `CargoToml::open` sets `inherited_version = true` on `version.workspace = true` (`cargo.rs:47-52`), and `current_version()` then returns `Err(ManifestError::WorkspaceInherited)` unless `ctx.cargo_workspace` carries a resolved version (`cargo.rs:178-189`). So with `cargo_workspace: None`, a maturin platform crate inheriting its version fails the whole plan_version run — the opposite of "opens successfully". Passing the ManifestDecl gate is necessary but not sufficient, and the criterion stops at the necessary half.

Fix: name `open()` and pin the context to apply.rs's own derivation (`apply.rs:118-130`), then add AC-002b fixing the inherited-version outcome (or declare it an error case and add the non_goal).

### Blocker 3 — AC-005 "empty for that group" has no observable truth value

`VersionPlan` (`plan.rs:14-26`) has no per-group partition; neither `PlatformWrite` (45-49) nor `OptionalDepUpdate` (51-55) carries group attribution. Rewrite to scope the workspace, not the group.

### Blocker 4 — AC-011 asserts on `active_ecosystems`, a function-local binding

`apply.rs:325-349` is local state no test can inspect. The observable equivalents are `ApplyOutcome.lockfile_refresh_results` (set at `apply.rs:406`) and `ApplyOutcome.staged` (assigned at `apply.rs:469`).

### What the spec earned (verified, not assumed)

- **Stale AC-ID cross-references: your corrections landed and the document is now internally consistent.** I checked every reference — `AC-009, AC-010, AC-011` for lockfile logic, `AC-008` for the malformed-manifest path, `AC-012, AC-012b, AC-013` for the precondition check, plus the non_goals citations. ### The mutation-testing report I was given was wrong

I was told lambda-mutator's run "did not complete" and to record it as `tool_unavailable`. That was false. The `cargo-mutants` process (PID 11538) was **still alive and running**, correctly scoped to exactly the four changed files. I let it finish rather than record a gap that didn't exist. It completed all 113 outcomes:

**42 caught, 32 timeout, 10 unviable, 28 survivors — and all 28 survivors are in pre-existing untouched code**: `cascade_action` (9, explicitly Track 9's scope per the spec's non_goals), `caret_covers` (8), `coverage` (1), and pre-existing `solve_cascade` regions at lines 195-336 (10). **Zero survivors in the new Fixed-group block, version.rs, snapshot.rs, or config/groups.rs.**

I checked that this wasn't vacuous — "no survivors" is worthless if no mutants were generated. **8 mutants were generated inside the new block (lines 384-434) and all 8 were detected.** The strongest evidence: mutants at lines 333 and 336 in the *pre-existing* Linked-group block **survived**, while their exact structural analogues at 404 and 407 in the new mirrored block **did not**. The new tests are strictly stronger than the code they were modeled on. The manual break-it-and-check verification is corroborated, not merely accepted.

### Two traps I had to avoid

**The exit code lied.** My first `cargo test ... | tail -60` returned exit 0 — but a pipeline returns *its last command's* status, so that 0 came from `tail`, not `cargo`. It was not evidence of anything. Re-run with `pipefail`: 361 lib tests + 22 suites, 0 failed, **0 ignored**. Same issue recurred on clippy and the workspace run, so I re-ran each capturing the true status directly: clippy exit 0 with zero warning lines, workspace **975 passed / 0 failed** across 54 suites, fmt/doc/wasm all exit 0.

**Pointers are not proof.** Rather than confirm the evidence pointers resolved, I checked whether the code at each location does what the criterion requires. The AC-001 test is genuinely *discriminating*: pre-fix it yields A=2.1.0/B=0.2.0 and fails on B. AC-012's "no assertions altered" I verified mechanically — the entire 12-commit range is **844 insertions and exactly one deletion**, and that deletion is `ws.tags()?,`, the inline-arg replacement AC-009 mandates. I also confirmed the AC-005 test isn't vacuous: if its packages weren't discovered, `Workspace::load` would fail on `MissingGroupMember` before the assertion loop.

### Gaps recorded (none blocking)

1. **Sibling gap:** `GroupTable::from_groups` (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs:259-289`) is a third, `pub`, re-exported membership-building path with **no conflict check**. Test-only today, so not a spec violation — the spec scoped the fix to `resolve` — but it can construct a `GroupTable` violating the invariant `resolve` now enforces.
2. **Newly-reachable pre-existing defect:** `fixed_group_target` hardcodes `SemVerVersioning`. The spec non-goals this, but wiring the block in changes its blast radius. In `plan_version` a mixed-grammar group is caught by `pre_mutation_checks` first; `plan_snapshot` deliberately does *not* call that check (AC-006), so a homogeneous all-PEP440 fixed group can now reach `SemVerVersioning.bump` and return `Err` — a failure path in `plan_snapshot` that did not exist before.
3. **Semver-breaking public API:** `CascadeInput` gained a required field and is re-exported from publishable `callisto-graph`. No in-workspace breakage (only two production construction sites, both updated), but external consumers break.
4. **Not run:** `moon run :audit` and the coverage-threshold gate.
5. **Test-robustness nits:** the AC-005 test asserts a version *prefix* rather than equality to one shared version and has no non-emptiness guard; the AC-014 test asserts only `is_err()` without pinning the variant, so an unrelated failure would satisfy it.

<result>I found a genuine, empirically-verified contradiction between AC-002b and the actual system behavior, and stopped before writing any implementation or committing. Here's what happened.

**Investigation**: I read TASK-3 from the plan and AC-002b/AC-007 directly from the spec file. TASK-2's landed code (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:264-302`) already loops over every `GroupMember::PlatformManifest` and derives `cargo_workspace` inheritance into `OpenContext`, confirming AC-007 (multi-sibling npm platform writes) is fully supported with zero new implementation.

For AC-002b (a maturin-style Cargo.toml platform manifest with `version.workspace = true`, discovered as a `GroupMember::PlatformManifest` through the real `Workspace::load` pipeline, per the spec's explicit "AC-001 scenario" wording), I traced the actual discovery code:

- `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:196-217` — the only code that registers a manifest into `IdentityIndex.platform` (which is what makes `groups.rs::resolve()` classify a config member as `GroupMember::PlatformManifest` rather than `GroupMember::Package`) is gated by `if *eco == Ecosystem::Npm`. There is no equivalent branch for `Ecosystem::Cargo`.
- I verified this empirically with a throwaway probe test (written, run, then fully reverted via `git checkout --`) that constructed a real workspace with a separate `crates/plat/Cargo.toml` (`version.workspace = true`, own package name `owner-darwin-arm64`) referenced in a `[[fixed-group]] members` list alongside the owner. Through the real `Workspace::load` → `plan_version` pipeline, it resolved as an ordinary `GroupMember::Package`, got its own independent `PlannedBump` writing to its own Cargo.toml, and `platform_writes` came back empty — never a `PlatformWrite`.

So there is currently no real-discovery code path that can produce a Cargo-format `GroupMember::PlatformManifest`, which AC-002b requires end-to-end. Per the spec's own non-goal #6 ("Validating that a GroupMember::PlatformManifest's owner resolves... this track assumes group config already passed that validation"), AC-002b's premise depends on discovery working for Cargo manifests — and it doesn't. Faking this via a hand-constructed `GroupTable` (bypassing real discovery) would contradict the task's own explicit instruction that these scenarios must be proven through `plan_version`'s real return value, not isolated calls — so I stopped rather than build a test/implementation that hides this gap behind a green checkmark.

I made no code changes (the probe was fully reverted; `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs` is clean at HEAD `4726863`) and did not commit.

<result>**Q1 — Match semantics.** Docs are unambiguous and internally consistent that `match` is PATH-based, not just an isolated example:

- `docs/00-design.md:1367,1379,1384`: worked example uses `match = "crates/*"`, `match = "packages/*"`, `match = "packages/special-case"` — real path-glob patterns, deliberately paired in the same example with NAME-based `members = ["foo", "foo-cli"]` for `[[fixed-group]]`/`[[linked-group]]` (so the doc distinguishes "match = path" from "members = name" on purpose, not by accident).
- `docs/01-spec.md:6331-6334` — §14's own formal algorithm: `if an explicit [[package]] whose match == P` and `for each [[package-set]] whose match glob ⊇ P`, where P is explicitly defined as "each discovered package P (by project root path, workspace-relative)" (line 6325). This is the spec's normative pseudocode, not just illustrative prose.
- No real (non-illustrative) config anywhere in the repo uses path-style patterns — the only hits are this one worked example.

The REAL shipped code (`config/pattern.rs`, `config/resolve.rs`) already does something different and coherent: `PackagePattern` matches by NAME glob with an optional `ecosystem:` prefix for disambiguation (`"cargo:pkg-*"` vs `"npm:pkg-*"`), backed by `PackageId::matches`, with a dedicated error (`BareRuleMatchesMultipleEcosystems`, `docs/01-spec.md:1572-1576`) telling the user to add an ecosystem prefix when a bare name-pattern is ambiguous across ecosystems. This is tested, working, and structurally exactly "name + publish-method(ecosystem) uniqueness."

**Q2 — GitHub Action JSON dependency.** Only two real `jq` sites parse callisto's own JSON output (as opposed to `gh` CLI output, which is separate and unaffected):

<result>## Report: Track 9 rewrite-key bug — scope investigation

**Directive**: investigate scope of the `RewriteKey.name` cross-ecosystem bug in `cascade.rs`.

**1. `CascadeInput` needs a new field, but that's not the real blocker.** `IdentityIndex` is not accessible via `solve_cascade`'s existing scope. Adding `identity: &amp;'a IdentityIndex` to `CascadeInput` (mirroring `tags: &amp;'a TagIndex`) is necessary but not sufficient — see #2.

**2. The real blocker: `plan_version`/`plan_snapshot` can't obtain `&amp;IdentityIndex` from `ws.graph` at all.** Both are generic — `plan_version&lt;R: CommandRunner, D: DependencyResolver, I: SeverityInference&gt;`, `plan_snapshot&lt;R: CommandRunner, D: DependencyResolver&gt;` — and `Workspace&lt;'a, R, D = ManifestWalkResolver&gt;`. `.identity()` is an inherent method on the concrete `ManifestWalkResolver` only, not part of the `DependencyResolver` trait (which lives in `callisto-model`, Layer 1, and cannot reference `IdentityIndex`, a Layer 2 type in `callisto-graph`, without violating CLAUDE.md's layer-isolation invariant). So `ws.graph.identity()` will not compile inside either generic function as-is. Two real options: (a) a new Layer-2-only trait (e.g. `HasIdentity`) added as a second bound on `D` everywhere `plan_version`/`plan_snapshot`/`solve_cascade` are generic — cascades into every test fixture's custom resolver needing to implement it too; (b) store `IdentityIndex` as a sibling field directly on `Workspace` (populated by `Workspace::load` from `walk::build`'s already-computed `index`, independent of `D`), and thread `&amp;ws.identity` into `CascadeInput` at the two real call sites. (b) is cleaner — no trait-bound changes, no layer violation — but still requires a `Workspace` struct field addition plus checking/updating every direct `Workspace { .. }` literal construction outside `::load`.

**3. Construction-site count**: 16 total `CascadeInput {` sites — 8 in `cascade.rs`'s own test module, 6 in `crates/callisto-graph/tests/cascade_tests.rs`, 2 real (`commands/version.rs:73`, `commands/snapshot.rs:54`). Same order of magnitude as Track 1's `tags` field addition (which touched 15 sites).

**4. Fix shape at the call site** (cascade.rs ~253-280): `eco` is already correctly derived from `edge.from` (the manifest being rewritten). The one-line fix is `name: input.identity.native_name(&amp;edge.to, eco).unwrap_or_else(|| edge.to.name()).to_string()`. Fallback to `edge.to.name()` when `native_name` returns `None` is the right choice — it's the current (buggy but non-crashing) behavior for the common case where no cross-ecosystem identity was ever registered, so this fallback is a pure improvement with no new failure mode.

**5. "Crashes outright" claim: still accurate in spirit.** `RewriteKey.name` flows into `update_dependency_spec` (`crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:300`), which returns `Err(ManifestError::DependencyNotFound)` (confirmed at lines 308/341/349/697) when the key doesn't match a real manifest entry — not a Rust panic, but a hard `Result::Err` that propagates via `?` through `apply_version_plan`, aborting the whole apply for that package. Not a literal crash, but a hard user-visible failure on exactly the scenario described (a real cross-ecosystem rewrite with mismatched native name).

**Bottom line**: this is NOT "narrow, single-function" as the master plan's tier assignment claimed. The actual code-level fix (one line, `native_name` lookup with fallback) is trivial, but making it *compilable* requires either a new cross-layer trait bound (touching 3+ generic function signatures) or a `Workspace` struct field addition plus `Workspace::load` changes — both are architecture-level changes on par with Track 1's `CascadeInput.tags` work, touching ~16 call sites. Recommend re-scoping to at least the same rigor as Track 1 (full canon pipeline or a carefully-planned multi-task lighter loop), not a single quick patch.</result>

**Confirmed: no overlap** with MatrixReport/PublishPlan — the Action's only two `jq` sites (`.platformTargets[].targets[].artifactName`, `.releases[]?.tagName`) are untouched by anything below.

**IMPORTANT CROSS-TRACK FINDING:** `TagReport`/`CreatedTag`'s mismatch is the *same underlying defect* as Track 4's "tag fabricated-sha" bug — `tag.rs:82` already computes `let already_existed = ws.tags()?.contains_tag(tag_str);` but the value is discarded; the doc's `CreatedTag` shape already specifies the fix (`already_existed: bool`, with explicit rationale: "An existing tag at a different sha is an error diagnostic, not a silent overwrite"). Whichever track lands first should own this field; the other must not duplicate it.

---

### StatusReport / StatusPackageRecord — MISMATCH (report.rs:298–336 vs spec:1883–1934)
- `has_changesets: bool` — **doc says mandatory** ("§12.5 mandates `.hasChangesets`; the field the Action's mode dispatch reads") — **entirely missing from the struct**.
- Doc's `StatusEntry` (renamed `StatusPackageRecord` in code, harmless) is missing `last_released_version: Option&lt;Version&gt;` and `release_trigger: ReleaseTrigger` — both absent from code.
- `changed_since_last_tag: bool` — doc says "Mandatory... v0.1 reports the fact" (always serialized); code has `skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not"`, silently omitting the field from JSON when `false`.
- Code has an extra field not in the doc: `pending_changesets: Vec&lt;String&gt;`.
- Construction sites: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/status.rs:105`, `crates/callisto-cli/src/render/mod.rs:311`.

### SnapshotReport — MAJOR MISMATCH, likely exception (report.rs:339–348 vs spec:1938–1962)
- Doc: `version: Version` + `packages: Vec&lt;SnapshotPackage{name, ecosystem}&gt;`.
- Code: `snapshot_tag: String` + `bumps: Vec&lt;BumpRecord&gt;` — **completely different field names, types, and shapes**, not a rename-level fix.
- **Flagging as likely exception**: this isn't "populate a field correctly," it's two top-level fields with different names *and* different types/semantics. Construction site: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/snapshot.rs:146`.

### ComposePrBodyReport — MISMATCH, borderline exception (report.rs:363–371 vs spec:1971–2018)
- `body` (doc) vs `pr_body` (code) → JSON key `body` vs `prBody` — a rename, not additive.
- `metadata: PrBodyMetadata` (labels/managed_labels/overflow — a whole label-tracking subsystem) is **entirely absent** from code.
- Flagging: the rename is a breaking change; the missing `metadata` object is more than a one-line fix. Construction sites: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/pr_body.rs:74,237`.

### ValidateReport — MISMATCH (report.rs:386–394 vs spec:2035–2045)
- `ok` (doc) vs `valid` (code) → JSON key rename.
- `diagnostics` — doc says mandatory/always-present here specifically ("entire payload *is* its diagnostics"); code has `skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty"`, contradicting that. Construction site: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/validate.rs:143`.

### TagReport / CreatedTag — MISMATCH, shares root cause with Track 4 (report.rs:409–437 vs spec:2049–2067)
- `tags` (doc) vs `created_tags` (code) → JSON key rename.
- `CreatedTag`: doc has `already_existed: bool` (missing from code — see cross-track finding above); code has an extra `package: PackageId` field not in the doc. Construction sites: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/tag.rs:65,74,103,113,120`.

### InitReport — MOST DIVERGENT, definite exception (report.rs:440–461 vs spec:2071–2087)
- Near-zero field overlap beyond `schema_version`/`diagnostics`. Doc: `locator: String`, `packages: Vec&lt;InitPackage&gt;`, `written: Vec&lt;PathBuf&gt;`, `proposed_config: Option&lt;String&gt;`. Code: `initialized: bool`, `config_path: PathBuf`, `diff: InitDiff{new_ecosystems, applied}` — none of these four exist in the other's shape.
- This reads as a genuine design evolution the docs never caught up with (same category as the Track 3a/6-doc/8-doc precedent), not a mechanical correctness fix — **recommend routing through a doc-correction-first check** (confirm which design actually shipped and is intended) before treating this as "correctness-fix, no version bump." Construction site: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs:190`.

**Net assessment against the resolved decision** ("correctness-fix the rest, no schemaVersion bump for these 7"): StatusReport's fixes are genuinely additive/correctness-shaped and fit the decision cleanly. SnapshotReport, ComposePrBodyReport's `body` rename, ValidateReport's `ok` rename, TagReport's `tags` rename, and InitReport all involve **renaming or wholesale-replacing existing fields**, not just adding missing ones — each is a real break for any existing consumer parsing the old key. Worth a quick decision-owner check on whether the "no version bump" assumption survives contact with these five before implementation starts.</result>

Headline: this revision fixed what the first audit found, and every file:line citation in the spec checks out against live code — I verified all of them myself rather than trusting the spec. It still fails, on six items, two of which are new.

The dominant one is the `--dry-run` path. All four tag criteria hinge on `contains_tag`, which is only reached when a permit exists (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/tag.rs:82`). With `--dry-run` the function takes the else-branch at tag.rs:53-80 and pushes `sha: release.sha.clone()` with no existence check, and `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/tag.rs:63` writes the same JSON report. The fabricated sha survives the fix through a shipped flag, and AC-06's verification ("by running `callisto tag`") doesn't say which mode to run in — so a tester using `--dry-run` on a fixture repo would fail a correct implementation.

That same gap makes the newly-added final `non_goals` entry factually wrong: the floating-major alias is *not* "unconditionally force-moved on every run" — on the dry-run path tag.rs:64-69 pushes the alias sha while `create_floating_major` is never called. That entry currently instructs a downstream planner to skip a live defect.

The other new-issue find worth calling out is the exit-code-0 hole: the minimal fix satisfying AC-03 and AC-04 as written lets 0 fall into the else-branch ending in `exit $STATUS_EXIT` (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml:96`), which is `exit 0`. With no `set -u`, `HAS_CHANGESETS` is unset, line 100 evaluates false, and the action publishes — silently, on an unrecognised exit code.</result>

## Two new blockers found in the fresh pass

**1 (critical) — the changelog read path ignores `Package.changelog`.** The spec mandates deriving `{pkg_dir}/CHANGELOG.md` from `pkg.manifests.first().path.parent()`. But `Package.changelog: Option&lt;PathBuf&gt;` (`package.rs:17`) is the already-resolved changelog path, always `Some`, and user-overridable — `walk.rs:388-392` sets it to `rel_path.join(override_path)` when a `[[package]]` rule specifies `changelog = "..."`. It is exactly what the **write** side uses (`version.rs:148`). The override is a supported, tested feature: `per_package_config_test.rs:63-99` asserts a configured package resolves to `RELEASES.md`, explicitly not `CHANGELOG.md`.

Implementing the spec as written means `callisto version` writes to `RELEASES.md` while `plan_publish` reads `CHANGELOG.md`, finds nothing, and emits a spurious `ChangelogSectionNotFound` — reintroducing the exact "silently reporting a missing changelog excerpt" defect the spec's purpose statement says it exists to eliminate. Affects AC-10, AC-10b, AC-11, AC-12, AC-12c, the `extract_section` api_surface entry, and the `scope` field.

**2 (major) — AC-12b is unconstructible and specifies wrong behavior.** Its fixture ("a publishable package with zero manifests") cannot exist: packages are built from `package_manifest_decls` (`walk.rs:322`), every entry carrying a non-empty `decls` — the same unconstructible-fixture class as the prior round's BLK-03. Meanwhile the empty-`pkg_dir` state *is* reachable, via a root-level manifest (`Path::new("Cargo.toml").parent()` is `Some("")`), a configuration actively tested at `walk.rs:798-812`. For those packages the root `CHANGELOG.md` is legitimately their own changelog, but AC-12b mandates not reading it — which would blank `changelogSection` for every single-crate and hybrid-root workspace, including this repo's own shape.

Both blockers share one root cause and one fix: switch to `Package.changelog` (in scope at the `ReleaseEntry` site — `publish.rs:423-428` is in the same `for pkg` loop as the pkg_dir code at `publish.rs:289-298`). That resolves the override bug and dissolves AC-12b's empty-directory case entirely.

One notable deviation worth flagging: the plan's exact test content stubbed `callisto` as `callisto() { exit ${stub_exit}; }`. In bash, calling `exit` inside a function called from the top-level script terminates the entire script immediately — it does not behave like a subprocess returning an exit code that `$?` can capture after `set +e`. This caused the RED-phase run to diverge from the plan's predicted output (AC-02 also failed, with empty captured output everywhere) rather than the predicted "AC-02 passes even on buggy code" pattern. I fixed the stub to use `return` instead of `exit`, re-verified the RED phase matched the plan's intended pass/fail pattern, and proceeded. This is a one-line change to the test harness mechanics only — the assertions and exit codes under test are unchanged from the plan.</result>

<result>## Report

**1. pr_body.rs vs render_section — CONFIRMED, requires real integration work, not a one-liner.**
`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/pr_body.rs` (322 lines) never imports or calls anything from `callisto_changelog` — confirmed via full read. It hand-builds a summary table + collapsible-details Markdown structure directly from `VersionPlan.bumps: Vec&lt;PlannedBump&gt;` (each with a single `Option&lt;BumpReason&gt;`), matching on `BumpReason` variants inline (lines ~104-123, ~185-225).

`callisto_changelog::render_section` (`crates/callisto-changelog/src/render.rs:5`) is structurally different: it renders ONE severity-grouped changelog section for ONE package's ONE version transition, from `ChangelogInput{package, from, to, entries: Vec&lt;ChangelogEntry&gt;}`. It has no concept of "all packages in this run" or of pr_body.rs's table/collapsible-details wrapper.

**Verdict: not a mechanical swap.** A real fix means calling `render_section` once per bumped package (building a `ChangelogInput` from each `PlannedBump`, mapping `BumpReason` → `ChangeSource` — logic that already exists in `commands/version.rs:157-195` and could be shared/reused) and embedding each package's rendered section inside pr_body.rs's own composition structure. This is data marshaling + reuse of existing mapping logic, not new business logic, but it is a genuine refactor, not a one-line change.

**2. ChangeSource::Commit / BumpReason::Inference — data ALREADY EXISTS, pure wiring gap.**
`InferenceOutcome` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/infer.rs:29-34`) already carries `commits: Vec&lt;(CommitSha, String)&gt;` — full per-commit sha+subject, not just a count. At the only construction site of `BumpReason::Inference` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:224-229`), only `outcome.commit_count` (a `usize`) is kept; `outcome.commits` (the real Vec) is discarded on the spot — never stored anywhere. No architecture change needed to surface it, just threading it through (e.g. add a representative-commit field to `BumpReason::Inference`, or carry the Vec separately to wherever `ChangeSource::Commit` needs to be built in `commands/version.rs`). No existing code/docs comment indicates which commit should be "representative" if multiple contributed — that's an open design choice, not a blocked-on-missing-data problem.

**3. ChangeSource::NewGroupMember — data ALREADY EXISTS, pure wiring gap.**
`pre_mutation_checks` (Track 1, already shipped) returns `GroupCheckOutcome.new_members: BTreeMap&lt;GroupName, Vec&lt;PackageId&gt;&gt;` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/groups.rs:14,85`) — exactly the `group: GroupName` data `ChangeSource::NewGroupMember` needs, per package. It's computed in `plan_version` (`commands/version.rs:87-93` as `group_check`) but only `group_check.diagnostics` is ever consumed (line 219) — `group_check.new_members` is computed and then never read anywhere in the function. Same verdict as #2: wiring gap, not missing data.

**4. ChangelogInput.entries union bug — CONFIRMED, root cause is upstream single-valued reason maps.**
At `commands/version.rs:148-154`: `if let Some(mut agg_input) = agg.changelog_inputs.get(id).cloned()` — changeset-sourced entries are used as-is (only `from`/`to` overwritten) when present; the `else` branch (lines 156-195, which synthesizes `ChangeSource` from `outcome.reasons.get(id)`) never runs when a changeset entry exists. So changeset-vs-synthesized is a hard if/else, not a union — this matches "changeset always wins over other sources" exactly.

Deeper root cause: `outcome.reasons`/`agg.reasons` are `BTreeMap&lt;PackageId, BumpReason&gt;` — single-valued per package by construction, all the way up through `cascade.rs`'s severity/reason bookkeeping. So even within the non-changeset branch, only one synthesized entry is ever possible per package regardless of how many real causes contributed.

**Scoped fix is achievable without deep architecture change**: `outcome.reasons.get(id)` is still readable inside the changeset branch (it's a separate map from `agg.changelog_inputs`), so the union fix can be: when a changeset drove the bump AND `outcome.reasons.get(id)` also holds a genuine non-changeset reason (cascade/peer-escalation/group-union), append a second synthesized `ChangelogEntry` to `agg_input.entries` alongside the changeset one. This closes the most common real-world case (changeset + cascade colliding) without touching the single-valued `reasons` maps upstream. A *full* multi-cause union (e.g. two cascades from different paths) would need `reasons` to become `Vec&lt;BumpReason&gt;` throughout cascade.rs — out of reach for a scoped fix, should be flagged as a known remaining limitation if the spec doesn't take it on.

**Summary for spec-scoping, mirroring the ComposePrBodyReport precedent:** unlike that case, all three "missing" pieces here (#2, #3, and the common-case union in #4) have real backing data sitting one hop away from where they're discarded — none require fabricating placeholder data. #1 is real integration work reusing existing mapping logic. The spec can require full implementation of all four rather than deferring any of them, though #4 should scope explicitly to "changeset + one other reason" and name the deeper multi-cascade-union case as an explicit non-goal.</result>

### Blocker 1 — AC-003 (primary)

Round 2's fix moved the defect rather than eliminating it. I enumerated the full state table `changelog_inputs {Some,None} × reason {9 variants}`. AC-005 requires `changelog_inputs` is `Some`; AC-006 requires `None`. **AC-003 constrains neither** — and `{Some, Inference}` is reachable:

`aggregate.rs` runs the inference loop *first* (223-236), setting `reasons[P] = Inference`. The later changeset loop overwrites the reason only when `entry.severity &gt; cur_sev` (:297) but pushes into `changelog_inputs` whenever `entry.severity != None` (:309). So a package with inferred Major + Patch changeset keeps `reason == Inference` **and** owns a changeset entry.

In that cell, `version.rs:149` takes the `agg_input` branch, AC-005 excludes Inference from its four enumerated reasons, AC-006 is excluded by `changelog_inputs == Some` — yet AC-003 still literally demands a `Commit` entry, saying nothing about whether the changeset entries survive. Secondary, same criterion: AC-003 says only "contains" and pins no count. AC-005 pins exactly N+1, AC-006 pins exactly 1 — AC-003 is the only synthesis criterion left unpinned, so leaving the catch-all `"Version bump (major)"` entry in place *and* appending `Commit` passes both mandated tests while emitting a junk changelog line.

Three required changes are spelled out in the blocker: add `agg.changelog_inputs.get(id) is None` to the precondition, pin both clauses to `entries.len() == 1`, and add `Inference` to AC-005's reason list with its explicit `ChangeSource` mapping plus a fourth test case.

### Blocker 2 — AC-004 (test-method rationale)

In that fixture the fresh member's reason is `BumpReason::Changeset`; `union_fixed` does not overwrite it because `aggregate.rs:421` only reassigns when `target &gt; cur`, and the fresh member is what set `target`. The changeset entry arrives via `version.rs:149`'s pre-existing branch, not AC-005 — so the fixture never exercises additive ordering against any spec-added entry, which is exactly what the parenthetical claims it proves. The length-free assertion lets both the described and a corrected fixture pass, leaving vector:planner free to build either. ### Round 3's two blockers are genuinely fixed

**(a) State table re-derived from live code.** `aggregate.rs:297` gates the reason overwrite on `entry.severity &gt; cur_sev` while `aggregate.rs:309` pushes into `changelog_inputs` whenever `severity != None` — so `{changelog_inputs: Some, reason: Inference}` is confirmed reachable. ### Two new blockers, both introduced or left by round 3's own corrections

**1. AC-003 now contradicts AC-004.** Round 3's fix added an unqualified "contains EXACTLY ONE entry" to both AC-003 branches. A never-tagged fixed-group member with `pkg.changelog`, no changeset, bumped by inference satisfies AC-003 *and* AC-004 simultaneously — AC-003 demands 1 entry, AC-004 demands the NewGroupMember append making 2. AC-005 and AC-006 both already carry the carve-out; AC-003 is the only one missing it.

**2. AC-004's new second test case is not constructible as described — and neither is the first.** This is the one I was asked to trace hardest, and the trace does not clear it. `new_members` is populated *only* from `groups.fixed` (`groups.rs:28`), so any AC-004 fixture is necessarily a fixed group, which means `solve_cascade`'s fixed-group convergence block always runs. That block computes the winner from the **already-released** member's base:

```rust
// groups.rs:129-135 — fixed_group_target
let aligned_base = if !released.is_empty() {
    base.get(&amp;released[0]).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| Version::semver(1, 0, 0))
} else { Version::semver(0, 0, 0) };
```

and then, at `cascade.rs:433-440`, overwrites the reason for any member whose target differs:

```rust
for id in member_ids {
    if out.targets.get(&amp;id) != Some(&amp;winner) {
        out.targets.insert(id.clone(), winner.clone());
        out.reasons.insert(id.clone(), BumpReason::FixedGroupUnion { group: g.name.clone() });
```

The fresh member's target came from `bump_target` on *its own* base. So unless the two members' manifest versions are identical, `reasons[fresh]` gets overwritten to `FixedGroupUnion` **after** the cascade sets it — which breaks case (2)'s asserted `DependencyUpdate` middle entry *and* case (1)'s premise that no AC-005 mapping applies (making it 3 entries, not the asserted 2). "A fresh, never-tagged member" naturally reads as a package at a different version from the released one, so the natural fixture is the failing one.

AC-004 does check for an overwrite — but only at `cascade.rs:501`, which is the wrong site (and is `sev &gt; cur_sev`, not `target &gt; cur_sev`; `target` is not the identifier there). The gate at 501 is real and correctly characterized; it just isn't the one that threatens the reason.

The fixture *is* constructible with one added constraint: both members at the same manifest version (e.g. 1.0.0), only the released one tagged. Then `bump_target(fresh, sev) == winner`, line 433 never fires, and both cases produce exactly the asserted sequences.

### Recommendation

Both blockers are one-sentence fixes and I've written the exact replacement text into the verdict file. But the retry budget is spent, and the pattern across all three rounds is identical — an absolute claim in a criterion that is false on a reachable state, each round's correction introducing the next one. That is a signal about the review loop, not about any single sentence. A human should apply the two fixes and clear it directly rather than sending it back through the gate a fourth time.</result>

## Key findings from live code
- `ReleaseEntry` struct: `crates/callisto-model/src/plan.rs` lines ~111-118 (fields `package`, `tag_name`, `sha`, `changelog_section`), `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`.
- Construction site: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs`, inside `plan_publish`, at the `releases.push(ReleaseEntry { ... })` block (~lines 505-510) — a `ver: &amp;Version` is already resolved and in scope there.
- `Version::is_prerelease()` already exists and is correct for both grammars: `crates/callisto-model/src/version.rs:126-131` — SemVer: `!v.pre.is_empty()`; PEP 440: `!v.is_post() &amp;&amp; (v.is_pre() || v.is_dev())`.
- `callisto-model`'s `Cargo.toml` license is `MIT OR Apache-2.0` with no AGPL dependency — layer isolation confirmed clean.
- Docs to update: `docs/01-spec.md` struct doc block (~line 1742) and a decision-table row (~line 2667, §M.12.2).
- Action loop to change: `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`'s `::group::5. Creating GitHub Release Entries` block (~lines 200-216).
- Test harness pattern to follow: `.github/actions/callisto-action/tests/test_status_check_branching.sh` (extracts the action's script body via `sed` between `::group::`/`::endgroup::` markers, stubs `gh`, asserts on captured args).
- No pre-existing REQ id covers this topic — the agent assigned `REQ-008` and flagged that a requirement@1 doc doesn't yet exist for it. Spec id assigned: `SPEC-005` (next unused after SPEC-002/003/004).
